<cite ref="Zevachim 64b:11">Zeb. 64ᵇ</cite> <he>צ׳ מלבר</he> the bird (whose head is to be pinched) must be turned outside (over the back of the priest’s hands).

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 79:6">Gen. R. s. 79</cite> <he>ציפור מבלעדי וכ׳</he> no bird is caught without the decree of heaven; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sheviit 9:1:13">Y. Shebi. IX, 38ᵈ</cite> <he>צפור</he>; <cite ref="Esther Rabbah 3:2">Esth. R. to I, 9</cite> <cite ref="R00423"><he>ציפר</he></cite>; <cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 10:8:1">Koh. R. to X, 8</cite> <cite ref="R00410"><he>ציפור</he></cite>, v. <cite ref="J00037"><he>יְבַד</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 4:6">Ib. to IV, 6</cite> (prov.) <he>טבא חדא צ׳ כפותא וכ׳</he> better one bird tied, than a hundred flying; a. fr.—Pl. <he>צִפָּרִין</he>, <he>צִפָּרַיָּא</he>, <cite ref="R00681"><he>צִפּוֹ׳</he></cite>, <cite ref="R00030"><he>צִי׳</he></cite>.

Targ. Ps. CIV, 17; a. fr.—Y. Shebi. l. c.; Gen. R. l. c., v. צַיָּידָא. Koh. R. l. c.; Lev. R. s. 3, beg., v. אֲגַר II; a. fr.—בֵּית צִפָּרַיָּיא (name of a family) Beth-Tsipparaya.
